ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Cars A and B travel on the same straight road. The relationship of their displacement x changing with time t is shown in the figure. It is known that car B makes uniformly accelerated straight-line motion, and its graph is tangent to the t-axis at 10 s. Which of the following statements is correct?
A. The initial velocity of car A is zero
B. The initial position of car B is at $x_0=60 \mathrm{m}$ [Source: Xue+Ke+Wang]
C. The magnitude of the acceleration of car B is $1.6\mathrm{~m/s^2}$
D. The two cars meet at 5 s, and at this time car B has the greater velocity

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Cars A and B travel on the same straight road. The relationship of their displacement x changing with time t is shown in the figure. It is known that car B makes uniformly accelerated straight-line motion, and its graph is tangent to the t-axis at 10 s. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of car B.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis is displacement x/m, and the horizontal axis is time t/s. The x-t graph of car A is a straight line starting from the origin and slanting upward to the right. The x-t graph of car B is a curve that bends downward from a larger displacement and gradually approaches the t-axis; the figure uses dashed lines to mark that the graphs of A and B intersect at t=5 s, x=20 m. The question stem states that the graph of car B is tangent to the t-axis at t=10 s. Reasoning: Car B makes uniformly accelerated straight-line motion, so its displacement function is a quadratic function of time. The graph of car B being tangent to the t-axis at t=10 s means x(10)=0, and the slope of the graph at that moment is 0, namely v(10)=0. Therefore, with t=10 s as the vertex, it can be written as x=1/2·a·(t-10)^2. When finding the magnitude of acceleration, take the absolute value. Substitute the point through which car B passes in the figure, t=5 s, x=20 m: 20=1/2·|a|·(5-10)^2=1/2·|a|·25, solving gives |a|=40/25=1.6 m/s^2.
